summary: Frontend-only testing of RoomFit Expo web preview (viewport 390x844). Covered the full demo wizard flow (Home → Upload → Dimensions → Furniture → Style → Budget → Layouts → Shop → Results). All testIDs from the spec render as expected and all primary happy-path flows pass: Start Designing / Try a Demo buttons, use-sample-floorplan-button renders sample-floorplan-svg, dimension validation (0.5 and 50 produce dimensions-error; m↔ft unit chip updates floor-area-text 17.3 m² ↔ 186 sq ft; apply-scale-button and apply-manual-dims-button work with dimensions-success), furniture add/remove and qty stepper (qty-armchair-plus pushes to 2× Armchair in furniture-summary-text), style multi-select, budget-input rejects <$300 (budget-error) and clears on valid value, 3 layout-card-* with layout-total and valid badges, regenerate-layouts-button advances to Set #2 and produces a different layout set, select-layout then layouts-continue-button navigates to shop. Shop page: shop-floorplan-svg + budget-bar-total/remaining render, shop-item-sofa-0 opens product-sheet with name/price/width/depth/height/retailer, swap-btn works, swap-result-message confirms success, and the budget-bar updates by the correct $50 delta (1,413→1,363, remaining 1,087→1,137). React Native issues detected: react-native-svg <G onPress> injects responder props on web producing a 'Unknown event handler onResponderTerminate' Console Error overlay in dev that interrupts navigation after swap (shop-continue-button → results was blocked by the dev error overlay). Also console warnings for deprecated 'shadow*' style props and 'props.pointerEvents' (RN 0.76+ API changes). One minor UX issue: tapping furniture-card-sofa once did not remove the sofa from furniture-summary-text (nested Pressable propagation).

ui_bugs.issue: Pressable/onPress on react-native-svg <G> leaks responder props (onResponderTerminate) to the DOM on web, triggering a React 'Unknown event handler property' Console Error overlay in dev. In my test this overlay appeared after a swap and blocked shop-continue-button → /plan/results navigation. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/FloorPlan.tsx:107

Single tap on furniture-card-sofa does not toggle qty from 1→0 reliably (summary still shows '1× Sofa'). Likely nested Pressable (priority-toggle) propagation on web. Reference: /app/frontend/app/plan/furniture.tsx:31-47

issues: Product sheet is tall bottom sheet on 390x844; swap-btn-* buttons sit below the fold and require scrolling inside the sheet. Consider making the swap list the primary scrollable area or sticky at top so swap action is reachable without scrolling.

react_native_issues.issue: onPress on <G> emits unknown DOM event handlers (onResponderTerminate etc.) on react-native-web. Replace with per-item <Pressable> hitSlop wrapper or move press handling to a transparent <Rect> with onPressIn/onPress. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/FloorPlan.tsx:107
Console warning: '"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow".' Audit components (likely Card/Button shadows). Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/ui.tsx
Console warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents.' Likely triggered by LinearGradient/Image. Audit usages.

action_items: Fix FloorPlan.tsx:107 — don't put onPress on <G>; wrap items in a <Pressable> or attach onPress to a top-level transparent <Rect> within the <G> to avoid leaking responder props to the DOM on web. This is HIGH priority because the dev error overlay intercepts clicks after a swap.

Investigate furniture-card tap-to-remove (plan/furniture.tsx): nested Pressable (priority-toggle) likely steals the gesture; use onStartShouldSetResponder or stop propagation (e.onPress stopPropagation on child, or convert outer wrapper to a non-Pressable row with an explicit tap target).
Replace deprecated 'shadow*' style props with 'boxShadow' and move pointerEvents from props to style across components.
Minor: Product sheet UX — swap buttons require scrolling in a tall sheet; consider making the sheet content scrollable with swap options higher up or sticky.
critical_code_review_comments: FloorPlan: putting onPress on react-native-svg <G> is unsafe on web; prefer onPress on an inner <Rect>/<Circle> that is already drawn.

furniture.tsx uses nested Pressable (card + priority-toggle inside). On react-native-web this bubbles; recommend stopPropagation on child Pressable's onPress or move the priority toggle out of the card's hit area.
budget.tsx: budget-input text state and plan state can diverge briefly (useEffect sync) — acceptable, no bug observed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Fresh install at https://roomfit-1.preview.emergentagent.com. Use viewport 390x844. Known deep-flow IDs: try-demo-button → upload-continue-button → confirm-dimensions-button → furniture-continue-button → style-continue-button → budget-continue-button → select-layout-<idx> (idx varies by seed; find the first with a select button) → layouts-continue-button → shop-item-<uid> opens product-sheet; swap-btn-* require scrolling inside the sheet (use element.scrollIntoView via page.evaluate before clicking). After a successful swap in dev builds, the react-native-svg Console Error overlay may appear and intercept subsequent clicks — reload or close the overlay to proceed. CSV download works via Playwright page.expect_download but can be blocked by the overlay.
rca_of_issue: Root cause for the dev error overlay: FloorPlan.tsx passes onPress={() => onPressItem(it.uid)} to a react-native-svg <G> element. On react-native-web, Pressable/onPress adds responder handlers (onResponderGrant/Terminate/etc.) which get forwarded as unknown DOM attributes to the <g> SVG element. React logs them as 'Unknown event handler property' which Expo's dev-mode LogBox surfaces as a full-screen Console Error overlay, blocking subsequent user interactions. Reproduction: open any FloorPlan with items that has onPressItem passed in (shop/results), then any navigation attempt may be blocked by the overlay. Mitigation: either (a) use an inner <Rect> with onPress and remove the <G onPress>, (b) render item hit areas as native <Pressable> absolute-positioned overlays using footprint coordinates, or (c) guard the onPress on <G> behind Platform.OS !== 'web'.
